import pandas as pd

def main():
    # File paths for the sources
    source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_85/test_0.csv"
    source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_85/test_1.csv"
    target_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_85/target_multisource_cot.csv"

    # Load Source 0
    # Schema: ['calaccess_committee_id', 'committee_name', 'calaccess_filing_id', 'date_received',
    #          'contributor_lastname', 'contributor_firstname', 'contributor_city', 'contributor_state',
    #          'contributor_zip', 'contributor_employer', 'contributor_occupation',
    #          'contributor_is_self_employed', 'amount']
    df0 = pd.read_csv(source0_path, dtype={
        'calaccess_committee_id': 'Int64',
        'committee_name': 'string',
        'calaccess_filing_id': 'Int64',
        'date_received': 'string',
        'contributor_lastname': 'string',
        'contributor_firstname': 'string',
        'contributor_city': 'string',
        'contributor_state': 'string',
        'contributor_zip': 'string',
        'contributor_employer': 'string',
        'contributor_occupation': 'string',
        'contributor_is_self_employed': 'boolean',
        'amount': 'float'
    })

    # Load Source 1
    # Schema: ['ocd_prop_id', 'calaccess_prop_id', 'ccdc_prop_id', 'prop_name',
    #          'ccdc_committee_id', 'calaccess_committee_id', 'committee_name', 'committee_position']
    df1 = pd.read_csv(source1_path, dtype={
        'ocd_prop_id': 'string',
        'calaccess_prop_id': 'Int64',
        'ccdc_prop_id': 'Int64',
        'prop_name': 'string',
        'ccdc_committee_id': 'Int64',
        'calaccess_committee_id': 'Int64',
        'committee_name': 'string',
        'committee_position': 'string'
    })

    # Step 1: Join Source 0 and Source 1 on calaccess_committee_id and committee_name
    # These two columns appear in both sources and are good join keys.
    # We do a left join of df0 (contributions) with df1 (prop & committee info)
    # to enrich contribution records with proposition and committee details.

    # To avoid ambiguity in committee_name columns, rename df1.committee_name to committee_name_y
    df1_renamed = df1.rename(columns={'committee_name': 'committee_name_y'})

    # Join keys: calaccess_committee_id and committee_name (df0.committee_name == df1.committee_name_y)
    # But df0.committee_name corresponds to df1.committee_name_y after rename.
    # So join on calaccess_committee_id and committee_name == committee_name_y
    merged = pd.merge(
        df0,
        df1_renamed,
        how='left',
        left_on=['calaccess_committee_id', 'committee_name'],
        right_on=['calaccess_committee_id', 'committee_name_y'],
        suffixes=('_x', '_y')
    )

    # Step 2: Select and rename columns to match target schema:
    # Target schema:
    # ['ocd_prop_id': string,
    #  'calaccess_prop_id': integer,
    #  'ccdc_prop_id': integer,
    #  'prop_name': string,
    #  'ccdc_committee_id': integer,
    #  'calaccess_committee_id': integer,
    #  'committee_name_x': string,
    #  'committee_position': string,
    #  'committee_name_y': string,
    #  'calaccess_filing_id': integer,
    #  'date_received': string,
    #  'contributor_lastname': string,
    #  'contributor_firstname': string,
    #  'contributor_city': string,
    #  'contributor_state': string,
    #  'contributor_zip': string,
    #  'contributor_employer': string,
    #  'contributor_occupation': string,
    #  'contributor_is_self_employed': boolean,
    #  'amount': float]

    # committee_name_x is from df0.committee_name (original committee_name in df0)
    # committee_name_y is from df1.committee_name_y (renamed from df1.committee_name)

    # Some columns may have missing values after join; keep as is.

    # Prepare final DataFrame with columns in order:
    target_columns = [
        'ocd_prop_id',
        'calaccess_prop_id',
        'ccdc_prop_id',
        'prop_name',
        'ccdc_committee_id',
        'calaccess_committee_id',
        'committee_name_x',
        'committee_position',
        'committee_name_y',
        'calaccess_filing_id',
        'date_received',
        'contributor_lastname',
        'contributor_firstname',
        'contributor_city',
        'contributor_state',
        'contributor_zip',
        'contributor_employer',
        'contributor_occupation',
        'contributor_is_self_employed',
        'amount'
    ]

    # Rename columns to match target:
    # df0.committee_name -> committee_name_x
    merged = merged.rename(columns={
        'committee_name': 'committee_name_x'
    })

    # Select columns, some come from df1 (joined), some from df0
    # If any target column is missing in merged, fill with NaN or appropriate default

    # Ensure all target columns exist in merged, add missing with NaN
    for col in target_columns:
        if col not in merged.columns:
            merged[col] = pd.NA

    # Reorder columns
    result = merged[target_columns]

    # Cast columns to target dtypes explicitly for consistency
    # Using pandas nullable dtypes where appropriate
    dtype_map = {
        'ocd_prop_id': 'string',
        'calaccess_prop_id': 'Int64',
        'ccdc_prop_id': 'Int64',
        'prop_name': 'string',
        'ccdc_committee_id': 'Int64',
        'calaccess_committee_id': 'Int64',
        'committee_name_x': 'string',
        'committee_position': 'string',
        'committee_name_y': 'string',
        'calaccess_filing_id': 'Int64',
        'date_received': 'string',
        'contributor_lastname': 'string',
        'contributor_firstname': 'string',
        'contributor_city': 'string',
        'contributor_state': 'string',
        'contributor_zip': 'string',
        'contributor_employer': 'string',
        'contributor_occupation': 'string',
        'contributor_is_self_employed': 'boolean',
        'amount': 'float'
    }

    for col, dtype in dtype_map.items():
        if dtype == 'boolean':
            # Convert to pandas nullable boolean dtype
            result[col] = result[col].astype('boolean')
        elif dtype == 'Int64':
            # pandas nullable integer
            result[col] = pd.to_numeric(result[col], errors='coerce').astype('Int64')
        elif dtype == 'float':
            result[col] = pd.to_numeric(result[col], errors='coerce').astype(float)
        else:
            result[col] = result[col].astype(dtype)

    # Step 3: Save to CSV
    # Use index=False to avoid writing row numbers
    result.to_csv(target_path, index=False)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
